newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian UES rises, heated market eases other shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian UES rises, heated market eases other shares.

text.p: Russian national utility UES rose on rosy first quarter profits in late afternoon trade on Thursday, but other leading shares eased as investors mulled record price levels.
Dealers said there was still support and a few predicted a rise in the market, albeit a slower one than seen over the past dozen or so days.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index slipped to 421.68, 2.64 percent off Wednesday's record 433.12 closing.
Thursday's modest $34.2 million total market turnover came nowhere near the record $94.3 million turnover seen Wednesday.

"Dealers are marking down prices, because they don't see any more bids," said Regent European Securities senior trader Dmitry Starenko. "Demand is mostly satisfied, but probably people are getting used to the new levels."
On the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX), traders said profit-taking had chipped into prices.

They said shares in UES, Russia's largest company by sales, firmed after UES reported first quarter pre-tax profits on an accruals basis rose to 369 billion roubles from 172 billion roubles a year ago.

UES, which firmed to $0.3595 at 1502 GMT from a daily low of $0.3505 earlier in the day and Wednesday's $0.364 closing, also helped boost its price by saying it planned to issue American Depositary Receipts this summer to allow foreign trade in its shares. It said it would also issue convertible bonds by autumn.
Russia's biggest oil company, LUKoil, dipped to $19.90 from $20.35, while regional power utility Mosenergo eased to $1.430 from $1.446. National bank Sberbank last traded at $296.00 from $302.00.
The closing prices were not official.
"We can see Western buys and Western sells but there's no excitement," said Menatep Bank's head of corporate securities, Sergei Kosynkin.
"Volumes are significantly less than yesterday, but you can't call them low. All the same people want to buy...prices could go up tomorrow but not so fast, so it will be quiet, even."
